discovery: Metamaterials, metasurfaces and plasmonics: engineering light-matter interaction at the subwavelength scale
motivation: These three physicists established the principle that optical properties need not be dictated by natural materials but can be designed through subwavelength structure. Pendry showed theoretically that artificial structures yield negative refraction, perfect lensing and transformation optics, founding the field of metamaterials. Capasso introduced optical metasurfaces and the generalized laws of reflection and refraction, enabling flat metalenses and wavefront control now entering commercial imaging and sensing. Atwater pioneered plasmonics as a discipline, showing how surface plasmons confine and guide light far below the diffraction limit, and applied these concepts to photovoltaics, tunable metasurfaces and optical devices. Together their work transformed optics from a science of given materials into one of engineered light-matter interaction, with profound impact on fundamental physics (superresolution, cloaking, strong light-matter coupling) and technology (imaging, communications, solar energy). Their discoveries are adopted by thousands of laboratories and industry worldwide.
